content: An antidiarrhoeal drug refers to any medication specifically designed to alleviate the symptoms of diarrhoea. Electrolyte solutions are utilized in acute cases of diarrhoea to replenish fluids and essential salts that have been lost due to excessive bowel movements. Bulking agents, such as methylcellulose, guar gum, or plant-based fibres like bran, sterculia, and ispaghula, are employed to manage diarrhoea associated with functional bowel disorders. These agents are also effective in regulating the output from an ileostomy. Absorbents are substances that bind to and neutralize toxic agents responsible for infective diarrhoea. Methylcellulose, in addition to being a bulking agent, also functions as an absorbent. Opiates are used to slow down intestinal transit, thereby reducing diarrhoea. Among these, loperamide is the most commonly prescribed because it effectively slows bowel movements without causing the typical narcotic side effects associated with other opiates.
